sections.h2: Who mails the Wayne County tax bill?
sections.html:
The commissioner on East Walnut Street mails it, and the assessors next door decide what the land and buildings are worth. The street address is 341 E Walnut St, Jesup, GA 31546. Letters go to PO Box 287 (ZIP 31598), and the phone is (912) 427-5910, staffed from 8:30 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon.

A single bill gathers money for five bodies: the State, Odum, Screven, the county government and the school system. Each of those sets its own millage, and the values come from the Chief Appraiser and Board of Assessors. Title on January 1 decides who receives the bill.

Reach the assessor at (912) 427-5920 about value, and the commissioner about payment, penalties or a payoff. Questions can go by email to taxcommissioner@waynecountyga.us. The commissioner's home page links the online payment site and the parcel search, and parcel records are also searchable through the county's qPublic page.

Wayne spreads across the Altamaha River country of southeast Georgia, with Jesup as the seat and Odum and Screven as the other cities. The county had an estimated 32,481 residents in July 2025, a rise of 7.8% over April 2020's 30,141, spread over roughly 642 square miles.

  • Homes: 13,180 units, two-thirds lived in by owners.
  • Value of the typical home its owner lives in (2020 through 2024): $162,800.
  • Midpoint rent: $846, with 102 construction permits in 2025.
  • Households: 11,061, and median household income of $53,427.

Bills for real estate and business personal property leave the office by September 15 and fall due November 15. Mobile homes run on a different clock: April 1, plus a 10% penalty after that. Vehicle tax follows the owner's birthday.

Interest begins the morning after the deadline and its rate is reset every January. A four-step penalty follows, starting at 5% once 120 days have gone by and rising on the same rhythm to a 20% cap. State code sections 48-2-40 and 48-2-44 govern the process.

Request a payoff dated for your closing day, because interest keeps adding. Unpaid property may be levied upon and in the end sold. Mobile home owners who dispute the value can return it to the assessors between January 1 and March 15.

The appeal address is Board of Tax Assessors, PO Box 174, Jesup, GA 31598, and the notice gives you 45 days from its mailing date. That notice shows the new value, the prior one, why it changed and an estimate of tax at the rollback millage. A complaint about the bill's size will not succeed, since only the value can be disputed.

The board looks again and reports its decision. Next comes a hearing before the county Board of Equalization, and Superior Court sits above that. Arbitration can replace the hearing, and the assessors will walk you through it.

Assessments equal 40% of market value. An owner may declare a figure of their own on a return during the January through April 1 window, and a refusal by the board opens the appeal. Real property returns roll forward at the previous value until the property changes.

You qualify by living in the home you own on January 1. Wayne has local exemptions, and where the local amount beats the state figure it takes over. The assessors take the application, and an approved one renews by itself until you move, sell or switch categories.

Call the assessor for the current filing cutoff before you rely on the exemption. A late filing waits for the next year's bill.

Standing timber has its own rule. It carries no tax until sold or cut, and the tax then uses its full value.

sections.h2: Other offices that matter in a sale
sections.html:
A few county departments, all with phone numbers in the 912 area code, are worth a call when a sale involves an estate, a tenant or a lien.

  • Probate Court, 427-5940, the first call when the house sits in an estate.
  • Magistrate Court, 427-5960, for landlord and tenant matters.
  • County administrator and commissioners, 427-5900, the general county line.
  • Sanitation Department, 427-5985, for pickup and landfill service at the address.
  • Extension Service, 427-5965, for well, septic and land questions.

Ask for the balance in writing ahead of closing and carry it as a line item. The bill belongs to the January 1 owner, so a house that changes hands in October still has a full-year charge, which the attorney divides between you and the buyer. The payoff figure tells the title company what to send.

  • Ask for balances on every open year, with penalty and interest.
  • Check whether the lot lies in Odum or Screven and picks up a city bill.
  • Confirm homestead status so the buyer knows whether to apply.
  • If the title company asks, the Clerk of Superior Court can supply your deed.
  • Ask whether a mobile home on the lot gets its own bill.

Heirs and landlords who have not looked at the account for years should do this early. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can have the county paid at closing, so old balances, repairs and tenant issues do not hold up the sale.

faqs.q: What phone number serves Wayne County taxpayers?
faqs.a: The commissioner answers at (912) 427-5910 from 341 E Walnut St in Jesup, and the assessor takes value questions at (912) 427-5920.

faqs.q: When is Wayne County real estate tax due?
faqs.a: Normally November 15, after a September 15 mailing. Mobile homes come due April 1.

faqs.q: How long is the Wayne County window to dispute a value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days counted from when the notice was mailed. Address it to PO Box 174, Jesup, GA 31598. It must dispute the value, since the size of the bill is not appealable.

faqs.q: What are the late charges on Wayne County tax?
faqs.a: Interest runs from the next day, a 5% penalty joins it after 120 days, and further steps follow at 120-day intervals up to 20%. The interest rate is reset each January.

faqs.q: What fraction of market value is taxable in Wayne County?
faqs.a: Forty percent of fair market value forms the assessed amount. Exemptions come off that amount, then the millage rate is applied.
